← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Captive-pin tool access: reference bodies and digital assumptions

Source review: 2026-10-14, Luna extra-high, read-only manufacturer-catalog research. Main-thread modeling owns dimensional adoption and the saved-solid access study. This is a geometric study of the existing nominal 3.175 mm pins and 6 × 1.2 mm formed heads; no heading process or stainless tooling capacity is qualified.

Published tooling dimensions

The retained Snap-on/ATI airframe tooling catalog is bound by its source manifest. Manufacturer PDF, with a separate ATI catalog reference.

ReferencePublished envelopeInterpretation
ATI108AN1/8, for 1/8-inch AN470 solid-rivet heads (PDF p. 34; printed p. 112)3/16-inch shank; 3/8-inch body diameter; 1/8-inch body lengthBody diameter converts exactly to 9.525 mm. It is not a specified cup-face diameter or complete squeezer.
ATI108AP1/8Same shank/body diameter; 1/4-inch body lengthSame 9.525 mm body-size reference, with a different body length.
ATI100A3-1/8 and related sets (PDF p. 30; printed p. 108)1/2-inch body diameter; 3.5-inch cataloged length, with a 5.5-inch variant; .401-inch shankBody diameter converts exactly to 12.7 mm; cataloged lengths convert to 88.9/139.7 mm; the primary catalog does not explicitly label them overall lengths. Nose cup, taper and gun/retainer envelope remain unspecified.

These are solid-rivet tools. Blind-rivet puller nosepieces use a different mechanism and were excluded. The catalog does not rate this custom stainless pivot-pin material or head-forming process.

Other useful, unadopted references are the USA Tungsten bucking-bar chart (ETBB39: 3.75 × .75 × .313 inches; ETBB20: 6 × 1 × .5 inches), its selection guide, and the Hanson rivet catalog, printed C84, with 3000C yoke reach/gap choices. Hanson's listed capacity includes 1/8-inch solid aluminum and 3/32-inch solid steel, so it does not establish 1/8-inch solid-steel or stainless capacity. These bar/frame dimensions are retained as research context, not modeled tool geometry.

Adopted digital envelopes

src/design_parameters.py:P5_TOOL_ACCESS controls three constant-diameter cylindrical approach envelopes:

  • 6 mm: project-selected head-sized approach, equal to the nominal formed-head diameter.
  • 9.525 mm: a body-sized sensitivity using the ATI squeezer-die diameter.
  • 12.7 mm: a body-sized sensitivity using the ATI air-hammer set diameter; used for representative CAD overlays.

Each cylinder starts at the saved pin's outer head face and extends outward along its signed hinge axis. Its length is at least 150 mm (design-selected), and is extended when needed to finish 10 mm beyond the furthest projected obstacle bounding box. The complete cylinder is intersected with saved BRep obstacles, so this declared straight nose sweep is continuous rather than a set of sampled translation poses. Final formed heads remain present; tangential contact with the target face is permitted, and every pin is included in collision checking.

The larger constant diameters at the head face are deliberate body-size sensitivities. Actual cup-face geometry and shoulder/taper may permit access that these cylinders reject. Passing or blocking one cylinder is not acceptance or rejection of a specific tool. Full tool holders, jaws, handles, operator access, fixture stiffness, weld beads, manufacturing variation and heading loads remain outside this check.

Four stages are tested for every gate end and diameter: isolated hinge hardware before wall attachment; isolated wall/gate module; completed insert on a bench; and completed insert in the nominal pan/pickup/tube proxies with its cover removed. The isolated hinge stage contains both fixed cheeks, the leaf and both moving cheeks, plus the captive pin. Its wall is explicitly absent because wall attachment is deferred. This tests an assembly-order hypothesis; an actual forming fixture and post-heading weld/fit process remain unresolved.

The study does not assert service access to unknown OEM mounting bolts or bosses. Pan-context results depend on the stated nominal proxies, and no vehicle interface coordinates are inferred from tool catalogs.
